# Step 2: Reuse

## Introduction

Check whether someone has already modeled your subject, and record what you found.

Reuse saves you work, and it makes your ontology easier to share. Even a "we looked and found nothing" is worth a note, because someone will ask later. You can read the full guide to this step in [Method](../../../../../docs/METHOD.md#step-2-reuse).

## What you'll make

One [design decision](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-design-decision), a note that explains a choice, saying you're starting from scratch and why.

## Run the commands

Run the [`okb reuse none`](../../../../../docs/CLI.md#cmd-reuse-none) command and give your reason:

```bash
okb reuse none --why "No coffee vocabulary is small enough to teach with, so this ontology starts from scratch. A real café would look at a food or beverage vocabulary first."
```

```text
Recorded that no existing ontology was reused, with your reason as a design decision.
```

## Read the output

- okb confirms in one line and keeps your reason with the ontology.
- A reader in a year can see that you looked, and why you chose not to reuse.

## Check your work

```bash
okb status
okb step next
```

```text
Espresso drinks  · 0 classes · 0 slots · 0 instances · 6 questions

✓ 2. Consider reusing existing ontologies ◀ you are here
     ✓ Reuse has been considered and recorded

Validator (steps 1–2): ✗ 0  ! 0  i 0   okb validate for details

Step 2 looks done. When you're happy with it: okb step next

Now on step 3. (To read a step's guide without moving: okb explain 3)

Step 3 of 8: Enumerate important terms

  Goal: Brainstorm every term you'd want to make statements about or explain to a user, without
  worrying yet about what kind of thing each one is.
  Why it matters: It separates what matters from how to model it. Trying to do both at once is
  the main reason beginners freeze.

Questions to answer
  • What are the things we'd like to talk about?
  • What properties do those things have?
  • What would we like to say about those things?
  • Read your competency questions: which nouns and verbs appear in them?

You're done when
  ○ At least 10 terms listed

Tips
  • Include nouns (wine, winery), adjectives and properties (color, body, sweet), and verbs
  (produces, goes well with).
  • Overlaps and duplicates are fine here. You'll sort them out in Steps 4 and 5.
  • Mine your competency questions and any documents you collected in Step 2.

In Ontology 101's wine example
  Terms in the wine example include wine, grape, winery, location, a wine's color, body, flavor
  and sugar content, fish, red meat and white wine.

Commands
  okb term add
```

> **Common mistakes**
>
> - **Letting this step stall you.** A quick search is enough for a first version.
> - **Skipping the record.** Step 2 isn't complete without it.

## Next step

You recorded that you're building from scratch, and why. Next, you'll brainstorm the words people use about coffee.
